title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-enhancement-v47
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: several customers have reported noisy utilization metrics and surprising burst throttling behavior during priority reshuffles. This PR consolidates burst-control telemetry with the dedicated fleet utilization reporting pipeline and adds a new priority-aware smoothing factor so that short-lived priority changes do not trigger aggressive throttles. Summary of changes: 1) Introduce priority-based burst_smoothing_coeff applied in tokenbucket and queueing layers to reduce transient throttles when priority promos/demotions occur. 2) Emit new metrics (dedicated.burst.smoothing_coeff, dedicated.burst.adjusted_throughput, dedicated.fleet.priority_rebalance_events) to the centralized reporting pipeline and wire them into the existing dedicated utilization aggregator. 3) Refactor autoscaler controller to expose the burst control decision as a single observable decision event (AutoscalerDecision) so the UI and alerting rules can attach without duplicating logic. 4) Add a dashboard JSON and operator docs with suggested alert thresholds and rollout guidance. Backwards compatibility: default smoothing_coeff is 1.0 (no-op) and behavior is opt-in via config flag in DedicatedCapacitySpec; existing customers see no change unless they enable priority-aware smoothing. Testing: unit tests for tokenbucket math and controller decision logic; integration test that simulates priority reshuffle bursts and validates no regression in throughput SLOs; end-to-end smoke run against a small dedicated fleet in staging. Rollout plan: merged behind a feature flag; rollout to Canary fleet first (2% of capacity) for 48 hours, then staged ramp to 25% and 100% after verification. Related: references ENG-2169 and PM-4321. Breaking change: none. Notes: this also surfaces a small refactor that reduces duplication between the old dedicated util reporter and the new priority reporter, which will simplify future SLO work.
